findings.text: Within the first three paragraphs, a newcomer can say what Athena is, what a study is, and why this page exists. The header also links straight to the next steps, so the opening does its job.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: A visitor to the Athena site lands on a page that is almost entirely about a different tool, firstmate. Athena's own value appears only as a demonstration of traceable citations. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets two sentences about it before thousands of words about firstmate.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and header "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project"

findings.text: The page uses "agent" in two ways. In the opening it means the AI coding tools that do the work, which the page later calls workers. Everywhere else it means only firstmate's own deciding AI. A newcomer reading the first bullet can take the wrong meaning into the transition cards.
findings.source: "Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents." vs Transitions: "'Decided by agent' always means firstmate's own deciding agent, never a worker."

findings.text: The next steps exist and are concrete. But they skip the clone step, list no prerequisites (for example a Rust toolchain or model API keys), and don't say which repository `athena ask` acts on. A newcomer would likely have to go to the GitHub README before the commands work.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: "Ship" is used before it is defined. When the glossary does define it, the entry is mostly circular, so a newcomer never gets a plain statement that a ship is a task meant to change code and deliver it.
findings.source: Words used first: "local-only landing ... The last step of a local-only ship"; Glossary "ship": "A kind of task, named next to scouts."

findings.text: The page says a term is defined "again in the Glossary", but the two definitions of captain differ. The glossary version could make it seem the captain matters only when yolo is off.
findings.source: Words used first: captain "The person who directs firstmate and decides whether finished work is merged"; Glossary: captain "The person who approves every PR merge and every local-only landing when yolo is off."

findings.text: The state, counter and transition sections are precise and well cited, but they are written for someone checking firstmate's internals, not for someone meeting the page for the first time. Exit codes, lock behaviour and pending-close replay results take up most of the page, and no short summary says what a newcomer should take away.
findings.source: States of a piece of work / Transitions / Counters sections

findings.text: The page is honest that the study only read firstmate's files and never ran it, which helps a newcomer judge how far to trust it.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "every claim is marked read" and "none was run"
